strings.d1.s0.name: MASP
strings.d1.s0.tips: Lina Bo Bardi's museum suspended in mid-air, with Van Gogh and Portinari on glass easels. Free on Tuesdays, and Paulista is car-free on Sundays.
strings.d1.s1.name: Avenida Paulista
strings.d1.s1.tips: The city's financial boulevard. On Sundays it is pedestrianised, with street musicians and Japan House.
strings.d1.s2.name: Bráz Pizzaria Paulista
strings.d1.s2.tips: São Paulo pizza (the world's second pizza city): thin crust, muçarela de búfala.
strings.d1.s3.name: Parque Trianon
strings.d1.s3.tips: A remnant of Atlantic forest on Paulista, with plenty of shade.
strings.d1.s4.name: Sesc Avenida Paulista Terrace
strings.d1.s4.tips: A free rooftop terrace with a city panorama, inside a cultural centre.
strings.d1.b0.name: Mocotó Vila Medeiros
strings.d1.b0.tips: A legend of northeastern Brazilian cooking. It's far out but worth it (Uber).
strings.d1.b1.name: Instituto Moreira Salles
strings.d1.b1.tips: A photography museum with a terrace on Paulista. Free entry.
strings.d2.s0.name: Mercado Municipal de São Paulo
strings.d2.s0.tips: A 1933 market with stained-glass windows. Try the mortadella sandwich (Hocca Bar, 300 g) and pastel de bacalhau (salt cod pastry), and sample exotic fruit (vendors are insistent).
strings.d2.s1.name: Catedral da Sé & Marco Zero
strings.d2.s1.tips: A neo-Gothic cathedral and the city's point zero. Nearby is Pátio do Colégio (founded 1554).
strings.d2.s2.name: Edifício Martinelli / Farol Santander
strings.d2.s2.tips: A 1929 skyscraper. Farol Santander has a viewing deck on the 26th floor and a skate ramp.
strings.d2.s3.name: Theatro Municipal
strings.d2.s3.tips: An imitation of the Paris Opera. Tours run Wednesday to Friday, on Ramos de Azevedo square.
strings.d2.s4.name: Edifício Copan
strings.d2.s4.tips: Niemeyer's wavy building with 1,160 apartments. See it from outside (the terrace may be closed), and visit Bar da Dona Onça.
strings.d2.b0.name: Bar da Dona Onça
strings.d2.b0.tips: Brazilian classics at the foot of Copan. Feijoada (black bean and pork stew) on Saturdays.
strings.d2.b1.name: Pinacoteca do Estado
strings.d2.b1.tips: A brick museum by Ramos de Azevedo with Brazilian art. Free on Saturdays, next to Luz station.
strings.d3.s0.name: Ibirapuera Park
strings.d3.s0.tips: The city's Central Park, with Niemeyer pavilions. Cycle, visit the lake and the Oca.
strings.d3.s1.name: Museu Afro Brasil
strings.d3.s1.tips: Afro-Brazilian culture inside the park: slavery and art.
strings.d3.s2.name: Figueira Rubaiyat
strings.d3.s2.tips: Steak under a giant fig tree, in the upmarket Jardins district.
strings.d3.s3.name: Rua Oscar Freire
strings.d3.s3.tips: Brazil's most luxurious street, with the Havaianas flagship store and Melissa.
strings.d3.s4.name: Museu da Imagem e do Som
strings.d3.s4.tips: A sound and image museum with pop exhibitions.
strings.d3.b0.name: A Casa do Porco
strings.d3.b0.tips: Among the world's 50 best. A pork tasting menu in the centre; book months ahead.
strings.d3.b1.name: Casa de Vidro
strings.d3.b1.tips: The architect's glass house in Morumbi. Reservation required.
strings.d4.s0.name: Beco do Batman
strings.d4.s0.tips: Batman Alley graffiti in Vila Madalena. It changes every week.
strings.d4.s1.name: Coffee Lab
strings.d4.s1.tips: A Brazilian coffee laboratory run by Isabela Raposeiras.
strings.d4.s2.name: Mercado de Pinheiros
strings.d4.s2.tips: A neighbourhood market. Try Comedoria Gonzales, Peruvian cuisine by Rodrigo Oliveira.
strings.d4.s3.name: Instituto Tomie Ohtake
strings.d4.s3.tips: Ruy Ohtake's purple and red building in Pinheiros, with free exhibitions.
strings.d4.s4.name: Bar São Cristóvão
strings.d4.s4.tips: A football-obsessed bar on Aspicuelta street, with a street party on Fridays and Saturdays.
strings.d4.b0.name: Feira da Praça Benedito Calixto
strings.d4.b0.tips: A Saturday antiques and crafts market with chorinho music.
strings.d4.b1.name: Bar Veloso
strings.d4.b1.tips: The city's best coxinha (chicken croquette) and caipirinha. Expect a queue.
strings.d5.s0.name: Liberdade
strings.d5.s0.tips: The largest Japanese community outside Japan, with red torii gates and lanterns. On Sundays there is a market at Praça da Liberdade.
strings.d5.s1.name: Aska Lamen
strings.d5.s1.tips: A small Japanese ramen shop. Expect a queue, and bring cash.
strings.d5.s2.name: Museu da Imigração
strings.d5.s2.tips: A former immigrant hostel (like Ellis Island), covering Italian, Japanese and Turkish-Syrian migration.
strings.d5.s3.name: Bixiga
strings.d5.s3.tips: Cantinas on Rua 13 de Maio, the Vai-Vai samba school, and the Nossa Senhora Achiropita festival in August.
strings.d5.s4.name: Cantina Famiglia Mancini
strings.d5.s4.tips: A cantina on Rua Avanhandava since 1980. Giant portions of pasta and a queue.
strings.d5.b0.name: Templo Busshinji
strings.d5.b0.tips: A Zen temple, as an alternative to a museum.
strings.d5.b1.name: Sujinho
strings.d5.b1.tips: A late-night steakhouse serving churrasco, open 24 hours.
strings.d6.s0.name: Embu das Artes
strings.d6.s0.tips: A colonial artists' town 27 km away. The weekend crafts market is the draw (shops only on weekdays). It's 1 hour by bus.
strings.d6.s1.name: Igreja Nossa Senhora do Rosário
strings.d6.s1.tips: A 1690 Jesuit church with a sacred art museum.
strings.d6.s2.name: Restaurante Os Girassóis
strings.d6.s2.tips: A restaurant in a colonial house serving feijoada and Minas Gerais cooking.
strings.d6.s3.name: Embu Antique and Rustic Furniture Shops
strings.d6.s3.tips: Wooden furniture and ceramics. Shipping is available.
strings.d6.s4.name: Parque Villa-Lobos
strings.d6.s4.tips: A park in western São Paulo on the way back, for sunset and cycling.
strings.d6.b0.name: Parque Estadual da Cantareira
strings.d6.b0.tips: Atlantic forest north of the city, with views from Pedra Grande. Nature instead of Embu.
strings.d6.b1.name: Casa do Sino
strings.d6.b1.tips: A cantina serving pizza and pasta.
strings.d7.s0.name: Parque Buenos Aires
strings.d7.s0.tips: A French-style garden for a neighbourhood morning.
strings.d7.s1.name: Padaria Santa Teresa
strings.d7.s1.tips: A padaria (Brazilian bakery) breakfast: pão na chapa (grilled buttered bread) and pingado (milky coffee). A farewell treat.
strings.d7.s2.name: Museu do Futebol
strings.d7.s2.tips: A football museum inside Pacaembu stadium, with Pelé and Garrincha. Interactive.
strings.d7.s3.name: Guarulhos International Airport
strings.d7.s3.tips: Uber takes 45-90 minutes in traffic. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Rua Augusta
strings.d7.b1.name: Museu do Ipiranga
strings.d7.b1.tips: The Independence Museum, restored in 2022. Gardens, as an alternative to football.
strings.note0: The metro is safe and clean (Bilhete Único). Uber and 99 are cheap. Traffic is terrible between 17:00 and 20:00. Guarulhos is 45-90 minutes away; Congonhas is in the city.
strings.note1: December to March is summer: 30°C with afternoon downpours (flooding). Carnival is at Anhembi in February. May to October is ideal.
strings.note2: SAFETY: In the centre (Sé, Luz, 25 de Março), keep your wallet in front by day; it is empty at night. Don't take your phone out on the street. Paulista, Jardins and Vila Madalena are relaxed.
strings.note3: Pizza 80-100 BRL, pay-by-weight restaurant 50, mortadella sandwich 40, padaria breakfast 30. A 10% tip is included. Pix and cards are accepted everywhere.
strings.note4: MASP is free on Tuesdays and Pinacoteca on Saturdays. Paulista is pedestrianised on Sundays. Book A Casa do Porco months ahead. Visit Embu at the weekend.
strings.note5: Coxinha, pão de queijo (cheese bread), pastel, mortadella, feijoada (Wednesday and Saturday), caipirinha. Japanese food in Liberdade.
